title: Ringed presentation comparison data
statement: For small ringed sites retain the original standard derived-category, module restriction, ringed presentation functor, equivalence, slice and local-completeness comparison records. RingedPresentationCore consists of an additive functor preserving finite limits, finite colimits and sequential colimits, with its regular-unit isomorphism, K-injective preservation and natural derived internal-Hom comparison. RingedPresentationEquivalenceCore consists only of a module equivalence with its forward regular-unit and derived internal-Hom comparisons; additivity, exactness, colimit and K-injective preservation will be derived from equivalence. All original records have literally their original fields and definitions; these are data for, not claims of, existence of a comparison. The actual element restriction is additive and preserves finite limits, finite colimits, sequential colimits and K-injective complexes, independently of those records; the named API theorems prove these properties from its two adjoints and exact extension by zero. Induced maps between element sites are continuous, and successive module restriction is canonically the direct restriction; both assertions are proved by the named API theorems.

proof.text: Retain the definitions and field types from RingedPresentationTransport verbatim in a publicly imported module, so subordinate comparison theorems can use them without importing their parent. Add the two records by listing exactly their data; no existence theorem, choice or postponed proof is used in any definition.

The actual element restriction is sectionwise additive. Its module extension adjunction makes it a right adjoint, and continuous-cocontinuous restriction makes it a left adjoint; this gives the asserted limits and colimits. Presheaf extension is a direct sum of fibres and preserves finite limits. Compose with exact module sheafification and use the canonical pullback isomorphism to obtain finite-limit preservation of module extension. It also preserves colimits by its adjunction and is additive. The right-adjoint K-injective theorem now applies to actual restriction. Continuity is the last assertion of element-site descent. Both successive module restriction functors are sectionwise identical, giving the identity natural isomorphism.
